def-van-hove-window-sequence:
## Definition

Fix an integer $d\ge1$. A **Van Hove sequence of spatial windows** is a
sequence $(W_n)_{n\ge1}$ of bounded Borel sets
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) in $\mathbb R^d$ with
$0<|W_n|<\infty$ for every $n$, $|W_n|\to\infty$, and
$$\frac{|(W_n+K)\setminus W_n|}{|W_n|}\longrightarrow0 \quad\text{for every compact }K\subseteq\mathbb R^d.$$
Here $|E|$ is Lebesgue measure when $E$ is Lebesgue measurable, and
$W_n+K:=\{x+y:x\in W_n,\ y\in K\}$. As part of the condition, each boundary
excess $(W_n+K)\setminus W_n$ in the display is required to be Lebesgue
measurable. Thus the window volume diverges while every fixed compact spatial
enlargement adds a negligible relative volume.
def-spatial-window-average:
## Definition

Let $(W_n)$ be a Van Hove sequence in $\mathbb R^d$ as in
[[def-van-hove-window-sequence]]. On a probability space
$(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ ([[def-probability-measure]]), let
$(X(s))_{s\in\mathbb R^d}$ be a real random field in the coordinatewise
sense of [[def-random-field-stationarity-covariance-and-variogram]]; its
coordinates are real random variables
([[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]) such that the map
$(s,\omega)\mapsto X(s,\omega)$ is measurable for
$\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d)\otimes\mathcal F$
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For $W_n$, assume that
$\int_{W_n}|X(s,\omega)|\,ds<\infty$ for almost every $\omega$. Define the
**spatial window average** on that full-measure event by
$$\bar X_{W_n}(\omega):=\frac1{|W_n|}\int_{W_n}X(s,\omega)\,ds,$$
and set it to $0$ on the measurable exceptional null set. Here $|W_n|$ and
the integral use $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure, and a sample path means the
function $s\mapsto X(s,\omega)$. The theorem
[[thm-van-hove-window-average-l2-consistency]] establishes this integrability
and measurability from its stated second-moment hypotheses.
thm-van-hove-window-average-l2-consisten:
## Statement

Let $X(s)$, $s\in\mathbb R^d$, be a jointly measurable real random field on a
probability space, with constant mean $\mu$ and finite second moments. Assume
it is wide-sense stationary in the explicit sense that
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X(s+h),X(s))=C(h)$$
for all $s,h\in\mathbb R^d$, and that $C\in L^1(\mathbb R^d)$. Let $(W_n)$ be
a Van Hove sequence from [[def-van-hove-window-sequence]]. Then each spatial
window average from [[def-spatial-window-average]] is well-defined, satisfies
$$\mathbb E[\bar X_{W_n}]=\mu,$$
and
$$\mathbb E\bigl[|\bar X_{W_n}-\mu|^2\bigr]\longrightarrow0.$$
Thus these averages are unbiased and converge to the mean in $L^2$. No
variance consistency for any other estimator, weak consistency, or central
limit theorem is asserted.
def-lattice-covariance-and-variogram-est:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$, let $(Y_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}$ be a real random field
([[def-random-field-stationarity-covariance-and-variogram]]) whose coordinates
are square-integrable real random variables on one probability space ([[def-probability-measure]],
[[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]],
[[def-moments-variance-and-covariance]], [[def-integers]]), and let
$V_n\subset\mathbb Z^d$ be
nonempty finite observation windows. Write $M_n:=|V_n|$ and
$$\bar Y_n:=\frac1{M_n}\sum_{j\in V_n}Y_j.$$
For a fixed lag $h\in\mathbb Z^d$, let
$$P_n(h):=\{j\in V_n:j+h\in V_n\},\qquad N_n(h):=|P_n(h)|.$$
Only indices $n$ with $N_n(h)>0$ are admissible for this lag.

When the field is wide stationary in the sense of
[[def-random-field-stationarity-covariance-and-variogram]], write its constant
mean as $\mu$ and its displacement covariance as
$C(h):=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_{j+h},Y_j)$, which is independent of $j$ by
wide stationarity and agrees with the supplier convention by covariance
symmetry. Define the **pair-count-normalized
raw-product covariance estimator** by
$$\widehat C_n(h):=\frac1{N_n(h)}\sum_{j\in P_n(h)}Y_jY_{j+h}-\bar Y_n^{\,2}.$$
This convention subtracts the square of the one global sample mean from the
pair-count-normalized raw product average; it is not the average of pairwise
sample-centered products.

For the second-moment component of order-two intrinsic stationarity in
[[def-random-field-stationarity-covariance-and-variogram]], suppose the increments
have finite second moments and
$\gamma(h):=\frac12\mathbb E[(Y_{j+h}-Y_j)^2]$
is independent of $j$; define the empirical **semivariogram** by
$$\widehat\gamma_n(h):=\frac1{2N_n(h)}\sum_{j\in P_n(h)}(Y_{j+h}-Y_j)^2.$$
thm-lattice-covariance-estimator-asympto:
## Statement

Let $(Y_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}$ be real square-integrable random variables with
constant mean $\mathbb E[Y_j]=\mu$ and lag-dependent covariance
$C(h)=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_{j+h},Y_j)$ independent of $j$. Let $(V_n)$ be nonempty finite
observation windows and assume that their sample means from
[[def-lattice-covariance-and-variogram-estimators]] satisfy
$\bar Y_n\to\mu$ in $L^2$. For each fixed $h\in\mathbb Z^d$ with
$N_n(h)>0$ eventually, the pair-count-normalized raw-product covariance
estimator satisfies
$$\mathbb E[\widehat C_n(h)]\longrightarrow C(h).$$

Separately, if the second moment of the lag-$h$ increment is independent of
$j$ and equals $2\gamma(h)<\infty$, then the empirical semivariogram from
[[def-lattice-covariance-and-variogram-estimators]] is exactly unbiased:
$$\mathbb E[\widehat\gamma_n(h)]=\gamma(h)$$
for every $n$ with $N_n(h)>0$. These are expectation statements only; they
assert no variance consistency, weak consistency, or central limit theorem.
lem-integers-lattice-is-discrete-lca-gro:
## Statement

For every integer $d\ge1$, equip $\mathbb Z^d$ with coordinatewise addition and
its discrete topology. Then it is a locally compact Hausdorff abelian
(topological) group. Every function from this discrete space to a topological
space is continuous.
lem-dual-of-zd-is-torus:
## Statement

Give $\mathbb Z^d$ the discrete topology and let
$\mathbb T:=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ be the multiplicative unit circle. The
map
$$\Psi:\mathbb T^d\longrightarrow\widehat{\mathbb Z^d},\qquad \Psi(z_1,\ldots,z_d)(k_1,\ldots,k_d):=\prod_{r=1}^d z_r^{k_r}$$
is a topological group isomorphism, where the dual has the compact-open
topology and $\mathbb T^d$ has the product topology.
lem-transport-lattice-spectral-measure-t:
## Statement

Let $\Psi:\mathbb T^d\to\widehat{\mathbb Z^d}$ be the homeomorphism from
[[lem-dual-of-zd-is-torus]], and let $\mu$ be a finite positive Radon measure
on $\widehat{\mathbb Z^d}$. Define
$$F(B):=\mu(\Psi(B))$$
for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb T^d$. Then $F$ is a finite positive
Radon measure on $\mathbb T^d$, and for every bounded Borel function
$g:\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb C$,
$$\int_{\mathbb T^d}g(\theta)\,F(d\theta) =\int_{\widehat{\mathbb Z^d}}g(\Psi^{-1}(\chi))\,\mu(d\chi).$$
def-regular-grid-periodogram-and-smoothe:
## Definition

Let $Y=(Y_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}$ satisfy the constant-mean,
lag-dependent-covariance conditions from
[[def-lattice-covariance-and-variogram-estimators]], with known mean $\mu$
(set $\mu=0$ for a centered field), and use the frequency torus $\mathbb T^d$
identified with $\widehat{\mathbb Z^d}$ by
[[lem-dual-of-zd-is-torus]]. Represent frequency coordinates
$\lambda\in[-\pi,\pi)^d$ by the circle tuple
$(e^{i\lambda_1},\ldots,e^{i\lambda_d})$; coordinates and integration are
periodic modulo $2\pi$ in each coordinate. For $n\ge1$, set
$$\Lambda_n:=\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}^d,\qquad N_n:=n^d,$$
and let the $n^d$ Fourier-grid frequencies be
$$\lambda_{n,q}:=2\pi q/n\pmod{2\pi},\qquad q\in\Lambda_n.$$
The known-mean **regular-grid periodogram** is
$$I_n(\lambda):=\frac1{(2\pi)^dN_n} \left|\sum_{j\in\Lambda_n}(Y_j-\mu)e^{-i j\cdot\lambda}\right|^2, \qquad \lambda\in\mathbb T^d.$$
Integration over $\mathbb T^d$ uses product angular Lebesgue measure on the
fundamental cube $[-\pi,\pi)^d$
([[def-product-measure-on-sigma-finite-spaces]]).

For smoothing, let $K:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous, even,
compactly supported, and satisfy $K(0)>0$. For $b>0$, periodize the rescaled
kernel by
$$K_b^{\mathrm{per}}(x):=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^d}b^{-d}K((x+2\pi m)/b).$$
Because $K$ has compact support, only finitely many summands are nonzero for
each fixed $x$, so this periodization is well-defined.
For $\lambda\in\mathbb T^d$, when the denominator is positive, set
$$w_{n,q,b}(\lambda):= \frac{K_b^{\mathrm{per}}(\lambda-\lambda_{n,q})} {\sum_{r\in\Lambda_n}K_b^{\mathrm{per}}(\lambda-\lambda_{n,r})}, \qquad \widetilde f_{n,b}(\lambda):= \sum_{q\in\Lambda_n}w_{n,q,b}(\lambda)I_n(\lambda_{n,q}).$$
The smoother is undefined when that denominator vanishes. Its target, when a
spectral density exists, is the density of the **lattice-sampled field on the
dual torus**; no unaliased continuous-space spectral-density target is part of
this definition.
thm-regular-grid-periodogram-fejer-expec:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$ and let $(Y_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}$ be real square-integrable
random variables with constant mean $\mu$ and lag-dependent covariance
$$c(h):=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_{j+h},Y_j),$$
independent of $j$. Assume the Axiom of Choice and Dependent Choice. Then there
is a unique finite positive Radon measure $F$ on the angular torus $\mathbb T^d$
such that
$$c(h)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}e^{ih\cdot\theta}\,F(d\theta), \qquad h\in\mathbb Z^d.$$
For the periodogram $I_n$ of
[[def-regular-grid-periodogram-and-smoother]], define the product Fejer kernel
$$\Phi_n(x):=\frac1{(2\pi)^dn^d} \left|\sum_{j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^d}e^{-ij\cdot x}\right|^2 =\prod_{r=1}^d\frac1{2\pi n} \left|\sum_{a=0}^{n-1}e^{-iax_r}\right|^2.$$
Then, for every $n\ge1$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb T^d$,
$$\mathbb E[I_n(\lambda)] =\int_{\mathbb T^d}\Phi_n(\lambda-\theta)\,F(d\theta).$$
The kernel is nonnegative and has integral one with respect to product angular
Lebesgue measure. The spectral measure and density here belong to the
lattice-indexed observations on the dual torus.
lem-fixed-grid-sampling-spectral-alias-i:
## Statement

Assume AC and DC. Let $X(s)$, $s\in\mathbb R^d$, be a real wide-stationary field with mean $\mu$ and covariance admitting the density representation
$$ C(h)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{ih\cdot\omega}f(\omega)\,d\omega,\qquad f:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty),\quad f\in L^1(\mathbb R^d), $$
where $f$ is a specified Borel representative. Fix spacing $\delta>0$ and sample $Y_j=X(\delta j)$, $j\in\mathbb Z^d$. On $Q=[-\pi,\pi)^d$ set
$$ g_\delta(\theta):=\delta^{-d}\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}f((\theta+2\pi k)/\delta). $$
This nonnegative measurable sum is finite almost everywhere, is in $L^1(Q)$, and defines a periodic density of the sampled field's unique torus spectral measure:
$$ c(h)=C(\delta h)=\int_Q e^{ih\cdot\theta}g_\delta(\theta)\,d\theta,\qquad \int_Qg_\delta=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f=C(0). $$
Thus for the angular periodogram of [[thm-regular-grid-periodogram-fejer-expectation]],
$$ E[I_n(\lambda)]=\int_Q\Phi_n(\lambda-\theta)g_\delta(\theta)\,d\theta =\int_{\mathbb R^d}\Phi_n(\lambda-\delta\omega)f(\omega)\,d\omega. $$
The general fixed-grid target is this aliased density, without any alias-free assumption. Where a pointwise density limit is claimed, a version continuous at the target must be specified; a spectral measure alone supplies no canonical pointwise density value.
thm-regular-grid-smoothed-periodogram-bi:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Dependent Choice, as in
[[thm-regular-grid-periodogram-fejer-expectation]]. Let the lattice spectral
measure from that theorem be absolutely continuous
with a specified bounded representative $f\in L^\infty(\mathbb T^d)$ continuous at the chosen target frequency $\lambda_0\in\mathbb T^d$.
Let $K$ and $\widetilde f_{n,b}$ be as in
[[def-regular-grid-periodogram-and-smoother]], and let $b_n>0$ satisfy
$$b_n\to0,\qquad n b_n\to\infty.$$
Then the denominator
defining $\widetilde f_{n,b_n}(\lambda_0)$ is positive for all sufficiently
large $n$, and
$$\mathbb E[I_n(\lambda_0)]\longrightarrow f(\lambda_0),\qquad\mathbb E[\widetilde f_{n,b_n}(\lambda_0)]\longrightarrow f(\lambda_0).$$
This is an asymptotic-bias statement only; it asserts no variance limit,
weak consistency, or central limit theorem.
cor-fixed-grid-unaliased-spectral-bias-u:
## Statement

Assume the model and AC/DC of [[lem-fixed-grid-sampling-spectral-alias-identity]]. Fix $\omega_0\in\mathbb R^d$, and put $\lambda_0=\delta\omega_0$ modulo $2\pi$. Suppose the pointwise periodized sum $g_\delta$ has a bounded torus representative continuous at $\lambda_0$, agreeing with that sum at $\lambda_0$. Use the kernel and bandwidths of [[thm-regular-grid-smoothed-periodogram-bias-vanishes]]. Define the physically normalized estimates at $\omega_0$ by
$$ \widehat f_n^{\rm raw}(\omega_0)=\delta^d I_n(\delta\omega_0),\qquad \widehat f_n^{\rm sm}(\omega_0)=\delta^d\widetilde f_{n,b_n}(\delta\omega_0). $$
Then the smoother is defined eventually and both expectations converge to
$$ a_\delta(\omega_0):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}f(\omega_0+2\pi k/\delta). $$
In particular, both have vanishing bias for the unaliased value $f(\omega_0)$ if and only if
$$ f(\omega_0+2\pi k/\delta)=0\qquad\text{for every }k\ne0. $$
This exact pointwise condition does not restrict the general aliased-target theorem. A sufficient global condition is that $f$ is continuous and supported in a compact subset of the open Nyquist cube $(-\pi/\delta,\pi/\delta)^d$, with $\omega_0$ in that cube. No variance, consistency or CLT conclusion is asserted.
